PETRA ZLATARIĆ-NOVOSEL
Machine Learning Engineer
Osijek, Croatia | petra.zlataric@example.com | +385 55 555 0606 | github.com/pzn-ml-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Machine Learning Engineer with 5+ years of experience in natural language processing (NLP) and document classification. Experienced in taking machine learning work from research and prototyping through production deployment, including model serving and production quality monitoring. PhD candidate researching Croatian-language processing, with a focus on named entity recognition in legal texts.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Machine Learning Engineer | Slavonica Document AI d.o.o., Osijek
03/2023 – Present
- Developed an automated classification model for incoming documents, including invoices, contracts and administrative decisions, achieving 94% accuracy across 23 classes for public-sector clients.
- Fine-tuned BERTić and XLM-R transformer models for named entity recognition on Croatian documents.
- Introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry; deployed models as FastAPI services in Docker containers on Azure ML and Azure App Service.
- Established production model quality monitoring for data drift, with weekly reporting.
- Mentor two students during professional internships.

Data Scientist | Baranjska Kreditna Banka d.d., Zagreb (remote from Osijek)
09/2021 – 02/2023
- Developed customer churn prediction models using gradient boosting and LightGBM for the sales team.
- Analysed customer complaint text and built topic classification models using TF-IDF with logistic regression, later using fastText.
- Produced SQL reports using the Oracle data warehouse.

Research Project Assistant | Faculty of Applied Informatics, Drava University
10/2020 – 08/2021
- Built a corpus of Croatian legal texts and annotated the data.
- Wrote Python scripts to support research work.

EDUCATION
PhD studies in Computer Science | Drava University | 2022 – Present
Research topic: Named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts

MSc in Computer Science | Drava University | 2020

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, scikit-learn, LightGBM, fastText, spaCy, pandas, NumPy, SQL, MLflow, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, Git, Linux

LANGUAGES
Croatian (native), English (C1), German (B2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, concise, professionally structured and easy to scan. It presents strong evidence of NLP, document classification, transformer fine-tuning, production deployment, model serving, cloud use and production monitoring. The quantified result—94% accuracy across 23 classes—provides useful impact. The experience chronology and education are credible and relevant. The main content limitation is that some production engineering details requested by the role are not explicitly represented, particularly data versioning terminology, pipelines and software-engineering practices. The CV also omits the 2024 publication included in the Original Candidate Information, which would strengthen the NLP profile.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses standard headings, chronological experience, plain text formatting and recognizable technology names, so it should parse reliably in most ATS platforms. Supported job keywords such as Python, MLflow, model registry, model serving through FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, Azure App Service, monitoring, NLP and transformer models are present. AI screening probability is medium-high for the requirements supported by the candidate's background, but lower for the overall role because the CV does not show chat assistants or RAG, feature engineering, data ingestion pipelines, or four full years specifically in a Machine Learning Engineer position. The skills list would be more ATS-effective if grouped into categories and if supported production concepts such as model serving, model monitoring and model registry were stated explicitly.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns strongly with the degree, Python, Azure, MLflow/MLOps, model serving, model monitoring, NLP, language-model fine-tuning and production deployment aspects of the role. The candidate also demonstrates relevant text-data preparation through building and annotating a Croatian legal-text corpus, and teamwork through mentoring interns. The candidate's material does not show experience with chat assistants or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), feature engineering, or data ingestion pipelines. The CV shows approximately three years and eight months in the explicitly titled Machine Learning Engineer role, although the broader experience exceeds five years; therefore the strict requirement for at least four years as a Machine Learning Engineer shipping systems to production is not clearly met. The document also does not demonstrate CI/CD, automated testing, or orchestration beyond MLflow. These are candidate-background gaps or unproven areas, not defects that can be solved by wording alone.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES: None identified; the CV does not contain apparent unsupported skills or experience when compared with the Original Candidate Information.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the supported production scope more explicit without claiming four years specifically as a Machine Learning Engineer. For example, change the second sentence to: "Experienced in taking NLP and document-classification models from research and prototyping through production deployment, including model serving, model registry and production data-drift monitoring." This uses terminology from the job ad while remaining supported by the current Slavonica role.
2. In the current Slavonica Document AI experience entry, revise the MLflow bullet to include the supported model-versioning concept: "Introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry; deployed models as FastAPI services in Docker containers on Azure ML and Azure App Service." If accurate based on the existing work, "model registry" can also be represented as "model versioning through the MLflow model registry"; do not claim broader dataset versioning.
3. In the Technical Skills section, replace the single undifferentiated list with ATS-friendly categories using only existing evidence. For example: "Languages: Python, SQL"; "ML/NLP: PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, scikit-learn, LightGBM, fastText, spaCy"; "Data: pandas, NumPy, Oracle data warehouse"; "MLOps and Serving: MLflow, model registry, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, Azure App Service"; "Tools/Systems: Git, Linux." This makes the production and MLOps match easier to identify.
4. In the Research Project Assistant experience entry, make the supported text-data preparation more searchable by changing the bullet to: "Built and annotated a corpus of Croatian legal texts; wrote Python data-preparation scripts to support NLP research." Do not describe this as a production data-ingestion pipeline.
5. Add a Publications section after Education using the publication present in the Original Candidate Information: "Zlatarić-Novosel, P. et al. (2024). Named entity recognition for Croatian administrative documents. Workshop on Slavic Language Processing." This strengthens the evidence for language-model and NLP expertise. Preserve the source's indication that the proceedings are fictional if this CV is being used in a context where that matters.
